chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn A'sham, who said:
I asked him about a man whose wife purified herself from her menstruation, and he said: 'If a man says to his wife,

key_terms.طَهُرَتِ اِمْرَأَتُهُ مِنْ حَيْضِهَا: his wife purified herself from menstruation

ai.seo_question: Does a husband's statement of divorce upon his wife's purification from menstruation count as a valid divorce if witnesses hear it?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the ruling of *Taliq* (conditional divorce) in Shia jurisprudence, establishing that the husband's declaration upon his wife's purification is binding even if witnesses merely hear the statement without formally testifying. The Imam’s rhetorical question emphasizes the practical necessity of finality, rejecting the state of *Mualqa* (suspended/undecided) to prevent legal ambiguity for the wife. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the efficacy of the spoken word in marital contracts when specific conditions are met.
